item.title: Kansas Shrine Bowl Announces Hall of Fame Class of 2026
item.description: The Kansas Shrine Bowl has announced the four member Hall of Fame Class of 2026 to be inducted Wednesday, May 6, 2026, at the Kansas Shrine Bowl Hall of Fame ceremony during the Coach Bill Snyder Family/Sunflower Chapter National Football Foundation Banquet in Lawrence, Kansas. Additional event details and ticketing information will be announced soon.

item.title: Kansas Profiles: Living in Kansas, working everywhere
item.description: Is Kansas the middle of nowhere? A place with nothing to attract people to come, live, work and play? Today we’ll meet a man who was born and raised in the western United States. As he transitioned to work remotely in his career, he has found he can do his work from virtually anywhere — and has chosen to live in rural Kansas.

item.title: Senate passes bill to force Kansas officials to turn over personal data
item.description: TOPEKA — The Senate on Monday passed a bill to force state officials to share Kansans’ personal data with the federal government.

item.title: Small business owners squeezed by Trump tariffs await Supreme Court decision
item.description: WASHINGTON — Aluminum cans rolling off Virginia cider maker Tristan Wright’s production line cost more because of increased tariffs on aluminum.

item.title: Big tobacco, Kansas lawmakers take on unauthorized vapes
item.description: TOPEKA — The Kansas Senate approved tougher regulations on vapes Wednesday in an effort to crack down on unlicensed products and eliminate advertisements geared toward children.

item.title: Leading through change
item.description: Change of seasons, change of crops, the progress of technology or even physical changes as we watch our families grow and age. Change is inevitable.

item.title: Pilots seek regulation changes to land seaplanes on Kansas waters
item.description: TOPEKA — Pilots and business owners asked legislators to pass a proposal allowing them to land seaplanes on Kansas waters, and they said economic development would likely follow.

item.title: USDA Opens Continuous CRP Signup; Additional Enrollment Periods Set for Spring
item.description: Signup is now underway for producers and landowners interested in enrolling acreage in the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Continuous Conservation Reserve Program (CRP), with the current enrollment period running through March 20.
